questions.question: The marked price of an article is Rs.1,280. If a shopkeeper sold the article at 12% profit after giving 30% discount, then the cost price of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of an article is Rs.1,280. If a shopkeeper sold the article at 12% profit after giving 30% discount, then the cost price of the article is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Marker Price (MP) = Rs.1280

Profit % = 12

Discount % = 30

Formulas used:

Discount % = Discount/MP × 100

Profit % = Profit/Cost Price × 100

Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

Cost Price = (Selling price × 100)/(100 + profit)

Calculation:

Discount % = Discount/1280 × 100 

⇒ 30 = Discount/1280 × 100

⇒ Discount = 128 × 3 = Rs.384

Selling Price = 1280 - 384 =  Rs.896

Cost Price = (Selling price × 100)/(100 + profit)

⇒ (896 × 100)/(100 + 12)

∴ CP = 89600/112 = Rs.800 

Alternate Method

Cost Price = MP × (100 - D)/100 × 100/(100 + P)

⇒ Rs.1280 × 70/100 × 100/112 = Rs.800

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs 600, a shopkeeper makes a profit of 20%. At what price should he sell the article to incur a loss of 20% ?
questions.questionHtml: By selling an article for Rs 600, a shopkeeper makes a profit of 20%. At what price should he sell the article to incur a loss of 20% ?
questions.solution:
Given 

Selling price of an article at 20% profit = Rs 600 

Formula Used 

Cost price = selling price/(100 + profit%) × 100 

Selling price = cost price/100 × (100 - loss%)

Calculation 

Cost price = (600/120) × 100 = Rs 500 

Selling price = (500/100) × 80 = Rs 400

∴ The selling price of an article at 20% loss is Rs 400

questions.question: Manjeet bought a second-hand motorbike for ₹22,000 and spent ₹3,000 on its overhauling and maintenance. He then sold it with 12% profit. If he had sold it for ₹500 less, then what would have been his profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: Manjeet bought a second-hand motorbike for ₹22,000 and spent ₹3,000 on its overhauling and maintenance. He then sold it with 12% profit. If he had sold it for ₹500 less, then what would have been his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
The total cost price occurred to Manjeet for the bike ⇒ 22000 + 3000 = ₹25000

The selling price = 25000 + 25000 × 12% = ₹ 28000

Had he sold the bike for ₹500 less, the selling price would have been ⇒ 28000 - 500 = ₹27500

Now, his profit percentage = \({{27500 - 25000} \over 25000} \times 100\%\) ⇒ 10%

questions.question: A tradesman marks his products 35% above the cost price and allows his customers 15% reduction on their bills. What percentage of profit does he make?
questions.questionHtml: A tradesman marks his products 35% above the cost price and allows his customers 15% reduction on their bills. What percentage of profit does he make?
questions.solution:
Given:

A tradesman marks his products 35% above the cost price and allows his customers 15% reduction on their bills

Formula used:

Selling Price = Mark price - discount

Profit = selling price (S.P.) – Discount

Calculation:

Let Cost Price = 100

Mark Price = 100 + (100 × 35)/100 = 100 + 35 = 135

Discount is 15%

⇒ (15/100) × 135

⇒ 20.25%

Selling Price = MP - discount

⇒ 135 - 20.25

⇒ 114.75%

Profit = 114.75 - 100 = 14.75%

∴ Percentage of profit is 14.75%

questions.question: Raheem sold a crockery set for Rs. 1,092 at a profit of 20%. What would have been the actual percentage profit or loss on it, if he sold it for Rs. 950 (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.questionHtml: Raheem sold a crockery set for Rs. 1,092 at a profit of 20%. What would have been the actual percentage profit or loss on it, if he sold it for Rs. 950 (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling price of a crockery set = Rs 1,092

Profit percentage = 20%

New selling price = Rs 950

Concept Used:

Cost price = 100 / (100 + Profit%) × SP

Profit Percentage = Profit / CP × 100

Calculation:

⇒ Cost price of the crockery set = \(\frac{100}{100+20}\times 1092\)

⇒ Cost price of the crockery set = \(\frac{5}{6}\times 1092\) = Rs 910

⇒ Now, when selling price is Rs 950,

⇒ Profit = SP – CP = 950 – 910 = Rs 40

⇒ Profit Percentage = \(\frac{40}{910}\times 100\) = 4.40%

Therefore, the profit percentage made on selling crockery set at Rs 950 is 4.40%.

questions.question: While selling an item, a businessman allows a 40% discount on the marked price and incurs a loss of 30%. If the item is sold at the marked price, profit will be _______.
questions.questionHtml: While selling an item, a businessman allows a 40% discount on the marked price and incurs a loss of 30%. If the item is sold at the marked price, profit will be _______.
questions.solution:
Given:

Discount Percentage = 40%

Loss Percentage = 30%

Concept Used:

Cost Price = \(\frac{100}{100-Loss\%}\times SP\)

Profit % = \(\frac{Profit}{CP}\times 100\)

Calculation:

⇒ Let the marked price be Rs 100

⇒ Selling price = 100 – 40% of 100

⇒ Selling price = \(100-\frac{40}{100}\times 100=100-40=60\) Rs

⇒ Loss percentage = 30%

⇒ So, Cost price = \(\frac{100}{100-30}\times 60\)

⇒ Cost price = \(\frac{100}{70}\times 60=\frac{600}{7}\) Rs

⇒ If item is sold at marked price, then

⇒ Profit Percentage = \(\frac{100-\frac{600}{7}}{\frac{600}{7}}\times 100\)

⇒ Profit Percentage = \(\frac{\frac{700-600}{7}}{\frac{600}{7}}\times 100=\frac{100}{600}\times 100=\frac{100}{6}=16\frac{2}{3}\) %

Hence, the profit percentage made by selling an item at marked price is \(16\frac{2}{3}\%\).

questions.question: Sohan sold a plot for Rs 2,55,000at a 15% loss. At what price should he sell the plot to gain a 10% profit?
questions.questionHtml: Sohan sold a plot for  Rs 2,55,000at a 15% loss. At what price should he sell the plot to gain a 10% profit?
questions.solution:
Given :

Sohan sold his plot at 15% loss for 255000 rupees 

Formula used :

Selling price(at profit) = Cost price + Profit on cost price 

Selling price(at loss) = Cost price - loss on cost price 

Calculations :

Let the cost price be 'C' 

According to the question 

Selling price = C - 15% of C 

255000 = C - 15% of C 

⇒ C = 300000 rupees 

Now Selling price at 10% profit 

Selling price = 300000 + 10% of 300000

⇒ 300000 + 30000 

⇒ 330000 rupees 

∴ Selling price at 10% profit will be Rs 330000.

questions.question: If two types of pulses costing Rs. 97 per kg and Rs. 105 per kg are mixed in the ratio of 5 ∶ 3, then what is the cost of the resulting mixture?
questions.questionHtml: If two types of pulses costing Rs. 97 per kg and Rs. 105 per kg are mixed in the ratio of 5 ∶ 3, then what is the cost of the resulting mixture?
questions.solution:
Given:- Cost price of first variety = Rs. 97

Cost price of second variety = Rs. 105

To find:- Cost of the resulting mixture

Concept used:- Concept of weighted average,

Mean or weighted Average = \(\frac{n_1 \times w_1+n_2\times w_2}{n_1+n_2}\)

Calculation:- Let the cost of resulting mixture be x,

The cost of resulting mixture = Average of the two quantities,

⇒ Cost of the resulting mixture = \(\frac{5\times 97+ 3\times 105}{5+3}\)

⇒ Cost of the resulting mixture = \(\frac{800}{8}\)

⇒ Cost of the resulting mixture = 100

 

.·. The cost of the resulting mixture is Rs. 100

questions.question: A seller sells two shirts for Rs. 3,360. The cost of four such shirts for the shopkeeper was Rs. 5,600. What is the profit/loss percentage on each shirt?
questions.questionHtml: A seller sells two shirts for Rs. 3,360. The cost of four such shirts for the shopkeeper was Rs. 5,600. What is the profit/loss percentage on each shirt?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Selling price of 2 shirts is Rs3,360

Cost price of 4 shirts is Rs5,600

FORMULA USED:

Profit = S.P. - C.P. 

Profit% = ( Profit/C.P.) × 100 

Where, S.P. = Selling price , C.P. = Cost price 

CALCULATION:

Here, Cost of 4 shirts = Rs5,600 

⇒ Cost of 1 shirt = 5600/4 = Rs1400

Now, Selling price of 2 shirts = Rs3,360

⇒Selling price of 1 shirt = 3360/2 = Rs1,680

Now, Profit =  Selling price - Cost price = ( 1680 - 1400) = Rs280

⇒ Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100 = (280/1400)× 100 = 20%.

Hence, there is 20% profit on each shirt.

questions.solution:

the cost price of 25 articles is equal to the selling price of 35 articles.

profit percent = \(\frac{{selling\;price - cost\;price}}{{cost\;price}}\) × 100

loss percent =  \(\frac{{cost\;price - selling\;price}}{{cost\;price}}\) × 100

questions.question: A man wanted to sell his cycle at 30% profit but actually sold it at 30% loss for ₹2,100. At what price (in ₹) did he want to sell the cycle to earn the profit of 30%?
questions.questionHtml: A man wanted to sell his cycle at 30% profit but actually sold it at 30% loss for ₹2,100. At what price (in ₹) did he want to sell the cycle to earn the profit of 30%?
questions.solution:
Given:

Profit = 30%

Selling price = Rs. 2100, when there is a loss of 30%

Concept used:

Selling price = Cost price - Cost price × loss%

Selling price = Cost price + Cost price × profit%

Calculation:

Let the cost price be Rs. A

Selling price = A – A × 30%

According to the question,

A – A × 30% = 2100

⇒ 0.7A = 2100

⇒ A = 2100/0.7

⇒ A = 3000

So, the cost price of the cycle = Rs. 3000

Now,

Selling price at 30% profit = 3000 + 3000 × 30%

⇒ Rs. 3900

∴ He wants to sell the cycle to earn a profit of 30% at 3900 (in ₹).

questions.question: A pen was sold for ₹28.75 at a profit of 15%. If it was sold for ₹25.75, then what would have been the percentage of profit?
questions.questionHtml: A pen was sold for ₹28.75 at a profit of 15%. If it was sold for ₹25.75, then what would have been the percentage of profit?
questions.solution:
Cost Price of pen =\(\frac{100}{100+Profit \%}× SP\) = \(\frac{100}{100+15}× 28.75\) = Rs 25 

Profit = 25.75 – 25 = Rs 0.75 

Profit % = \(\frac{Profit}{CP}× 100\) = \(\frac{0.75}{25}× 100=3\%\)

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought a table for ₹4,600 and a chair for ₹1,800. He sells the table with 10% gain and the chair with 6% gain. Find the overall gain percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper bought a table for ₹4,600 and a chair for ₹1,800. He sells the table with 10% gain and the chair with 6% gain. Find the overall gain percentage.
questions.solution:
Selling price of table = 4600 + 4600 × 10/100 ⇒ 5060

Selling price of chair = 1800 + 1800 × 6/100 ⇒ 1908

Total selling price = 5060 + 1908 ⇒ 6968

Total cost price of table and chair = 4600 + 1800 ⇒ 6400

Gain = 6968 - 6400 ⇒ 568, Now, gain % = (568/6400) × 100 ⇒ 71/8 = \(8\frac{7}{8}\)

questions.question: Ram bought a cell phone and paid 30% less than its original price. He sold it at 50% profit on the price he had paid. The percentage of profit earned by Ram on the original price was:
questions.questionHtml: Ram bought a cell phone and paid 30% less than its original price. He sold it at 50% profit on the price he had paid. The percentage of profit earned by Ram on the original price was:
questions.solution:
Let's say the original price of the cell phone is "100M".

 Price Ram paid(CP) = 100M × 70/100 = 70M 

Selling price(SP) = (150 × 70M)/100 = 105M 

Profit = 105M - 100M = 5M 

Percentage of Profit = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100

⇒ (5M / 100M) × 100 = 5%

questions.question: P buys an article for Rs.280 and sells it to Q at a profit of 25%. Q sells it to R at some profit. R sells it to S for Rs. 560 making a profit of 40%. What percentage profit (rounded off to the nearest integer) did Q make?
questions.questionHtml: P buys an article for Rs.280 and sells it to Q at a profit of 25%. Q sells it to R at some profit. R sells it to S for Rs. 560 making a profit of 40%. What percentage profit (rounded off to the nearest integer) did Q make?
questions.solution:

R sells to S for Rs560, Profit% = 40%

Now, as Q sells it to R. So, S.P. of Q = C.P. of R = Rs400 

Now, S.P. of Q = Rs400 , C.P. of Q = Rs350

Profit = ( S.P. - C.P. ) = ( 400 - 350 ) = Rs50  and Profit% = (50/350) × 100 = 14.28% ≈ 14%

questions.question: If 11 oranges are bought for Rs 10 and 10 oranges are sold for Rs 11, what is the profit or loss percentage?
questions.questionHtml: If 11 oranges are bought for Rs 10 and 10 oranges are sold for Rs 11, what is the profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

Cost price of 11 oranges is Rs.10 

Selling price of 10 oranges is Rs.11 

Formula used:

Gain = Selling price – Cost price 

Gain% = (Gain/CP) × 100

Where CP is the cost price.

Calculations:

Cost price of an orange = 10/11

Selling price of an orange = 11/10 

Gain = (11/10) – (10/11) = 21/110  

Gain% = ((21/110)/(10/11)) × 100

⇒ 21%

∴ The gain percentage is 21%

questions.question: The profit earned by selling an article for Rs. 832 is equal to the loss incurred when the article is sold for Rs. 448. What will be the selling price of the article if it is sold at a 10% loss?
questions.questionHtml: The profit earned by selling an article for Rs. 832 is equal to the loss incurred when the article is sold for Rs. 448. What will be the selling price of the article if it is sold at a 10% loss?
questions.solution:
Given:

The selling price at profit = Rs. 832

The selling price at loss = Rs. 448

Required loss = 10%

Formula used:

S.P. = (100 - Loss%)/100 × C.P.

Where, C.P. = Cost price; S.P. = Selling price

Calculation:

Let, the profit = loss = x

So, 448 + x = 832 - x

⇒ x + x = 832 - 448

⇒ 2x = 384

⇒ x = 384/2 = 192

∴ The cost price = (448 + 192) = (832 - 192) = Rs. 640

So the selling price = (100 - 10)/100 × 640 = Rs. 576

∴ The selling price of the article will be Rs. 576
